newsitem.title: HAITI: 180 Haitian refugees feared dead at sea.
newsitem.headline: 180 Haitian refugees feared dead at sea.

text.p: Police, government and United Nations officials said they were investigating a report on Wednesday that some 180 Haitians disappeared at sea after leaving the Caribbean nation on an illicit trip to the United States early this month.

On Wednesday independent Radio Metropole reported that family members of the missing Haitians on Tuesday attacked a couple who had allegedly arranged the trip. The radio report said Rene Vis, of Petit Goave, and his wife barely escaped a lynching when police intervened.

Yannick Longchamps, a woman who said she boarded the boat in Petit Goave on Nov. 3 and then decided it was too crowded, told Reuters there were at least 180 people on board, including some 40 children.
"I am happy I got off the boat but I am very sad for all those children and some friends of mine who went even though the boat was overcrowded," said Longchamps.
Longchamps said each passenger paid $100 to take the trip. She said a man named Rene who arranged the voyage refused to reimburse her when she decided the trip was too risky.
"I wanted to go to Miami because I have a child in school and I don't have work," she said. "I thought it would be easier to find some kind of work in the United States."

Longchamps said word that the boat had arrived safely at the Western island of La Gonave came about four days after the boat departed. But fears that the boat might have sunk began to circulate after weeks passed without word from the passengers.
Information about the incident was sketchy, especially due to recent firings of top staff at the National Office on Migration (ONM).

Angry refugees demonstrated outside of the ONM offices and carried out a hunger strike over the past week to protest the firings. "We were fired for political reasons," said Privat Precil, the ex-director general of ONM.

Residents of the southern port city reported seeing personal belongings of those on the boat floating near the coast about a week after the boat departed, despite reports the boat had arrived safely in La Gonave.
The poorest nation in the hemisphere, Haiti lacks a reliable communications infrastructure, particularly in rural areas, which makes investigation more difficult.
Officials now staffing the ONM office said they had received no formal report about the boat.
